rv.q: The sumptuous fragrance of live cooking of traditional Persian ash-e-reshteh heightens this already impactful one-woman show.

Powered by Dina Soltan's agile solo performance, Chris White's arresting production of My English Persian Kitchen conjures a vivid world of oppression and resistance inside a mostly bare black box theater.
In the end, My English Persian Kitchen is an imperfect meal: warm and surprising, but overly bitter at points—to me, at least.

cn.t: Critics largely praise *My English Persian Kitchen* for Dina Soltan's agile solo performance and its poignant blend of cooking and storytelling, though responses vary slightly in enthusiasm.
